ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figures, two triangles of different sizes are each chosen and overlaid as in Figure 1 (with the right-angled vertices coinciding). It is given that $ \angle A=45^\circ$, $ \angle CDE=30^\circ$, and $ CE:BC=1:\sqrt{6}$. After rotating $ \triangle DCE$ $45^\circ$ clockwise around point $ C$, line $ ED$ intersects line $ AC$ at point $ O$. What is the ratio of $ OA:OC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw OF $\perp$ CE through O,\\
by the property of rotation, we have $\angle$OCE$=45^\circ$,\\
in $\triangle OEF$,\\
since $\angle$CDE$=30^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle$OEF$=60^\circ$,\\
therefore OF$=EF\tan\angle$OEF$= \sqrt{3}EF$,\\
thus OF$=CF= \sqrt{3}EF$, and $OC=\sqrt{OF^{2}+CF^{2}}=\sqrt{6}EF$,\\
therefore CE$=EF+CF= (\sqrt{3}+1)EF$,\\
therefore $\frac{CE}{OC}=\frac{(\sqrt{3}+1)EF}{\sqrt{6}EF}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{6}}$,\\
since CE$\colon BC=1\colon \sqrt{6}$,\\
thus $\frac{BC}{OC}=\frac{BC}{CE} \cdot \frac{CE}{OC}=\sqrt{6} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{6}}=\sqrt{3}+1$,\\
thus $\frac{OA}{OC}=\frac{AC-OC}{OC}=\frac{AC}{OC}-1=\frac{BC}{OC}-1=\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$,\\
thus $OA\colon OC=\sqrt{3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There are two schematic diagrams in the figure. In Figure 1, in the large triangle ABC, AC is vertical and BC is horizontal, the right-angle vertex is at C, A is above C, and B is to the left of C; the small triangle DCE shares the right-angle vertex C with the large triangle, CE goes left along BC, and CD goes upward along AC. Figure 2 shows that after the small triangle DCE is rotated clockwise around C, point E falls near the upper left of C, point D falls at the upper right of C, and the rotated straight line ED intersects the vertical line AC at O. Then reason: Set coordinates according to the specified method. Let C=(0,0), A=(0,L), B=(-L,0). Because ABC in the figure is right-angled at C, and ∠A=45°, AC=BC=L. Let the original CE=s, then E0=(-s,0). In the right triangle DCE, ∠CDE=30°, and CE is the side opposite 30°, therefore DC=√3s, so D0=(0,√3s). Rotate E0 and D0 clockwise around C by 45°, obtaining E=(-s/√2, s/√2), D=(√3s/√2, √3s/√2). Let O be the intersection point of the straight line ED and AC, and AC is the y-axis x=0. Take the parametric point E+t(D-E) on segment ED; its x-coordinate is -s/√2+t((√3+1)s/√2). Set it equal to 0, obtaining t=1/(√3+1). Thus the y-coordinate of O is s/√2+t((√3-1)s/√2)=s/√2·(1+(√3-1)/(√3+1))=√6s/(√3+1), so OC=√6s/(√3+1). Also CE:BC=1:√6, therefore L=BC=√6s, and AC=L. Thus OA/OC=(AC-OC)/OC=AC/OC-1=√6s/(√6s/(√3+1))-1=√3. Therefore OA:OC=√3:1.
